cards.text: Last time, Joab killed Abner in Hebron (2 Samuel 3:27). Abner was the commander of Saul's army, the man who made Saul's son Ish-bosheth king over Israel (2 Samuel 2:8-9). Now that news is headed straight for Ish-bosheth, and friend, this is NOT a "good morning" text.

cards.question: Ish-bosheth son of Saul hears that Abner has died in Hebron. How does he take it?
Ish-bosheth is the only one in Israel who is shaken by the news about Abner.

cards.text: Saul's son has two men who lead raiding parties: Baanah and Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite. Hang on to those names, friend, because this chapter is about to be ALL about them.

cards.question: Which tribe are Baanah and Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from?

cards.text: Then the writer leans over with a side note: Beeroth is considered part of Benjamin, because the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have lived there as foreigners to this day. Even the Bible stops to explain the family map, and friend, I RESPECT that.

Hold that thought on the brothers, friend, because the writer just hit PAUSE to tell us about Jonathan son of Saul's son. The boy was five years old when the report about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel, and his nurse picked him up and fled.

cards.question: As the nurse hurries to escape with Jonathan's five-year-old son, what happens to the boy?

answers.text: He is captured on the road
He is left behind in Jezreel

cards.question: Jonathan's son, the boy who fell, is named ___.

cards.text: And we're BACK to Rechab and Baanah. The brothers set out and show up at Ish-bosheth's house in the heat of the day, and friend, I've got a bad feeling about this.

cards.question: Rechab and Baanah arrive in the heat of the day, while the king is taking his midday ___.
How do Rechab and Baanah get into the interior of Ish-bosheth's house?

answers.text: As if to get some wheat
As if to bring him a report
As if to guard his room

cards.text: Inside, they stab him in the stomach, the same way Joab killed Abner (2 Samuel 3:27). Then Rechab and his brother Baanah just... slip away.
Here's the rest of what happened in that house. Rechab and Baanah went in while Ish-bosheth was lying on his bed, and after they killed him, they took something with them.

cards.question: What do Rechab and Baanah take from Ish-bosheth?
Rechab and Baanah travel all night by way of the Arabah and bring Ish-bosheth's head to David at ___.

cards.text: They tell the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life." I bet these two think they're about to be named employees of the month.

cards.question: Rechab and Baanah tell David what the LORD has done for him today. What do they say?

answers.text: Granted him vengeance on Saul's family
Paid him back for Abner's death
Given him peace with all of Israel

cards.text: But David answers them with an oath, by the LORD who has redeemed his life from all distress. Friend, that is NOT how an "attaboy" starts.

cards.question: David reminds Rechab and Baanah of the man who told him Saul was dead and thought he was bringing good news. David says he rewarded that man with a gift.

cards.text: David seized that man and put him to death at Ziklag. And David says it plain: "That was his reward for his news!"

cards.question: David tells Rechab and Baanah that wicked men have killed a ___ man in his own house and on his own bed.

cards.text: David says he will require Ish-bosheth's blood from their hands. So David commands his young men, and they kill Rechab and Baanah, cut off their hands and feet, and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron.

cards.question: What do David's young men do with the head of Ish-bosheth?

answers.text: Bury it in Abner's tomb in Hebron
Return it to Mahanaim for burial
Hang it by the pool in Hebron

cards.text: Saul's son is gone. But keep your apron on, friend, because David's road to the throne still has more in the oven.

findings.problem: Joab and Saul appear for the first time in this lesson, and neither is identified. Joab is named as Abner's killer with no word on who he is (the commander of David's army, 2 Samuel 2:13). Saul is mentioned only as 'Saul's army' and is never introduced.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: David first appears here, at Hebron, and is never introduced. The baker isn't told who he is or that he reigns as king in Hebron (2 Samuel 2:4, 11). That context matters, because the brothers address him as 'the king' and deliver Ish-bosheth's head to him.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Nothing sets up how the brothers get inside, so 'As if to get some wheat' can only be picked by luck. Card 10 says only that they show up at the house. Across both stops, about half of the choice cards are discovery questions: stop 1 cards 5, 9 and 12, and stop 2 cards 2, 3 and 11. That is more than 'a few.' At least this card needs more setup or a different question.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Card 1 says only that they 'took something with them.' Nothing helps the baker choose between head, crown and spear, so the pick is luck. The crown is an especially strong pull because the Amalekite took Saul's crown (2 Samuel 1:10).

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The joke 'explain the family map' doesn't match the fact. The side note in 2 Samuel 4:2-3 is about where the Beerothites settled and which territory Beeroth belongs to, not about family. The image mixes geography and family and won't click instantly.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'Jonathan son of Saul's son' is hard to read. It can be taken as 'Jonathan, the son of Saul's son.' Plainer: 'Jonathan's son (Jonathan was Saul's son).'

The story-isn't-over line says 'David's road to the throne still has more in the oven.' That hints at what comes next, which is David reaching the throne over Israel, instead of only saying the story isn't over.

rule.text: It gives nothing away about what happens next.

findings.problem: The opening card begins 'Last time, Joab killed Abner,' which assumes the baker did the previous passage in the story group. papa-dorin.md says he doesn't know how the baker has done before. The opening-card rule allows giving context, but it doesn't say whether that context can be framed as something the baker already saw.
findings.question: In a story group, can the opening card refer to the previous passage as 'last time,' or should outside context always be given without assuming the baker did the earlier lesson?
